hook.line: It's Vale's birthday this week, and a birthday in Colombia comes with a stream of wishes. You already have the verb shape for them; all you need is the word that starts a wish.
hook.es: Ojalá Vale no sepa nada de la fiesta.
hook.en: I hope Vale doesn't know anything about the party.

examples.en: I hope it doesn't rain on Saturday.

examples.es: Espero que te guste la torta.
examples.en: I hope you like the cake. (to a friend)
I hope there's cake for everyone.
I hope you're well. (to a friend)
I hope you get better soon. (formal)
I hope you can come. (to a friend)

rule:
Last week you used the wish forms after *quiero que*. Hoping works the same way, because a hope is a wish too.

*Ojalá* + wish form: *Ojalá no llueva.* No *que* needed.
*Espero que* + wish form: *Espero que te guste.*

English says I hope it doesn't rain, with an ordinary verb. Spanish can't: *Ojalá no llueve* sounds broken. After *ojalá* and *espero que*, the verb always takes the wish shape: *llueva*, *guste*, *estés*, *haya*.

The same rule as before: if it's your own action, there's no *que*. *Espero verte pronto.* I hope, I see you.

You've been saying the short versions for months without knowing it. *¡Que te mejores!* and *¡Que te vaya bien!* are wishes with the first part cut off: (I hope) that it goes well for you. Learn those whole for now.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the present subjunctive of wishes (*subjuntivo desiderativo*). *Ojalá* comes from Arabic, roughly "God willing".

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *llueve* or *llueva* and type the whole sentence: *Ojalá no ___ el sábado.* (I hope it doesn't rain on Saturday.)
Pick *gusta* or *guste* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *Espero que te ___ la torta.*
yourTurn.answer: Espero que te guste la torta.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I hope you're well.
yourTurn.why: *Estar* becomes *esté*, and for *tú* it's *estés*, accent and all.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I hope there's cake for everyone.
accept: Espero que haya torta para todos.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I hope to see you soon. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: You're the one seeing, so no *que*: just the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to don Hernando (formal) instead: *Espero que te mejores pronto.*
yourTurn.why: For *usted*, *te* becomes *se* and the ending loses its *s*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about you all: *Espero que te guste.*
yourTurn.why: For a group, *te* becomes *les*; one thing liked, so *guste* stays.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Ojalá* always wants the wish form: *llueva*.
A hope isn't a fact yet, so Spanish uses the wish form, *guste*.
When it's your own action, drop *que* and use the plain verb.
*Estás* is a fact; a hope takes *estés*, and the *tú* can go.

personal: Write two wishes for someone you know: one with *Ojalá* and one with *Espero que* (*Ojalá mi hermana...*, *Espero que mi amigo...*).
